text:
Andrea: Heads-up — CI started failing on the audit-event golden set job in the last deploy. Failing assertion is in audit-schema-checker: 'actor.id' missing, got 'actor_email' instead.
Jamal: Saw that too. Repro locally by running `./scripts/ci/golden-check.sh` against the latest canary image.
Lucas: I have the failing diff output if anyone needs it: 
```
-  "actor": { "id": "usr_123" }
+  "actor": { "email": "ops@example.com" }
```
Looks like some newer events are shipping email instead of id.
Priya: That aligns with the RBAC change rolled yesterday — we changed the session principal emission for service tokens to `principal.email` to simplify audit reads. We should have migrated validators.
Andrea: Ok so two issues: schema drift (field rename) and golden fixtures don't include the new shape. Also noticed some events now include `kms.encrypted_key_id` metadata that the validator rejects because it wasn't in the spec.
Olivia: Customers are asking about the KMS key id being included. Product wants to ensure that any KMS metadata is non-sensitive and can be surfaced in audit. Is that allowed?
Andrea: KMS key id is non-secret but we need to standardize the field name. Current event has `metadata.kms_key` while some infra code writes `kms.encrypted_key_id`. We should normalize.
Jamal: Short term: update golden fixtures to accept both `actor.id` OR `actor.email`, and allow the optional `kms.*` fields. Add a compatibility check to the validator so CI fails only if neither actor.id nor actor.email present.
Lucas: I'll open a QA PR that updates the goldens and adds the unit test case for `actor.email`. I'll run the golden-check locally once Andrea or Priya ack the acceptable schema.
Priya: Long term we should avoid schema branching. Proposal: add `actor.identifier` (string) to the canonical schema and deprecate `actor.id`/`actor.email` in favor of that. Migration plan = accept either for 3 releases, then require `actor.identifier`. Also add `event.meta.kms_key_id` canonical name.
Andrea: Sounds reasonable. Two action items: 1) immediate CI patch to reduce noise, 2) RFC to standardize field names and timeline.
Jamal: For (1) I'll put up a small PR that relaxes the JSON Schema validator to use `anyOf` for the actor fields. Example snippet: 
```
"actor": {
  "anyOf": [
    { "required": ["id"] },
    { "required": ["email"] },
    { "required": ["identifier"] }
  ]
}
```
That should be limited to the CI branch until we release the RFC.
Andrea: Perfect. Also add a check that flags presence of `kms.encrypted_key` blobs so we can audit for accidental secrets. For now only allow `kms_key_id` and `kms_key_metadata` as strings.
Olivia: Product note: We'll need messaging to customers if we change canonical fields. Prefer additive first (actor.identifier) with backwards compatibility.
Lucas: QA checklist: update golden fixtures generator to normalize these fields, add tests for both schema variants, and include an integration test that simulates KMS-encrypted payloads but with key id stubbed. I can add a mocked decryptor in test harness.
Priya: Also, our CI golden-check job should capture which commit last updated goldens and include a link. devops-bot can post a reminder when any PR touches `goldens/` folder.
devops-bot: noted — I can add a watcher that comments on PRs that modify `goldens/` and tag `@qa` and `@sec-eng`. Want that enabled?
Andrea: Yes please.
Jamal: Quick mitigation: adding `|| true` to the golden-check script is not acceptable. We should keep CI strict. The validator relax change should be a targetted JSON Schema tweak, short-lived.
Andrea: I'll draft the RFC for canonicalization today. Lucas/Jamal/Priya — can you pair on the temporary validator patch so we can get the pipeline green?
Lucas: On it, will open PR with updated goldens + tests.
Jamal: I'll review and include the `anyOf` validator change.
Priya: I'll update the infra emitter to write both `actor.identifier` and the legacy field for now (emit both keys). Also will standardize `event.meta.kms_key_id`.
Olivia: Thanks — please add a short customer-facing line to the RFC describing why the change improves auditability.
release-bot: Deploy job queued: build/canary-2141. Will run golden-check after deployment.
Andrea: Final note — add a small CI job that verifies golden fixture generation is deterministic (seeded randomness). We wasted time chasing nondeterministic UUIDs in fixtures earlier. Lucas, can you add seeding to the generator?
Lucas: Yep, will add `--seed` flag and update the CI invocation to pass `--seed=ci-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}`.
Andrea: Great. Thanks everyone. I'll create the RFC and link PRs here when they're up.
Jamal: Thanks — ping me when the validator PR is ready and I'll prioritize review.
Lucas: PRs: #4213 (goldens + tests), #4214 (schema relax). Opening now.
Andrea: Linking them here once available — closing thread for now.
